instruction: Proofread the document. Fix the known spelling, grammar, punctuation, word-choice, and style mistakes while preserving meaning, tone, paragraph ids, and intentional wording everywhere else.

issues.description: An unmatched quotation mark is inserted, creating a delimiter error.

expectedCorrection.find: Every law imports, "that something is to be done;
expectedCorrection.replace: Every law imports, that something is to be done;

issues.description: A plural determiner 'these' is incorrectly replaced with the singular determiner 'this' before a plural noun.
Misspelling 'supposed' as 'suposed', creating a nonword.
The subject and auxiliary verb are incorrectly ordered after the negative word 'Neither', failing to apply the required subject-auxiliary inversion.

expectedCorrection.find: Neither it can properly be said
expectedCorrection.replace: Neither can it properly be said

issues.description: Incorrectly forms a double superlative by adding '-est' to an adjective that is already modified by 'most'.
A space is missing between 'ever' and 'combine'.
An unmatched opening quotation mark is incorrectly inserted before 'extraordinary'.
Replaces 'affectation' with the visually similar but semantically incorrect word 'affection'.
An apostrophe is incorrectly added to the plural noun 'nations', creating a false possessive.
An unnecessary resumptive pronoun 'it' is inserted after the relative pronoun 'which'.

expectedCorrection.find: power which it can be applied

issues.description: The word 'sentiments' is incorrectly replaced with the similar-sounding word 'sediments', creating a malapropism.
The auxiliary verb 'have' is omitted, resulting in a grammatical error.

Inserting the subordinating conjunction 'that' before the interrogative pronoun 'what' creates an ungrammatical double subordinator (complementizer) for the embedded clause, resulting in a clear subordination error.
Replaces 'disposition' with the phonetically similar but semantically incorrect word 'deposition'.
The word 'there' is incorrectly replaced with its homophone 'their'.
An incorrect coordinating conjunction ('and') is inserted before the relative pronoun ('on which'), creating a coordination error since there is no preceding relative clause to coordinate with.
Incorrectly capitalizes the common noun 'execution' in the middle of a sentence.
An unnecessary word ('if') is inserted after 'whether', creating an ungrammatical sequence.
The past tense 'wrote' is incorrectly used instead of the past participle 'written'.
Replaced the plural pronoun 'They' (referring to 'nations') with the singular pronoun 'It', which incorrectly points to 'The case' and creates a pronoun reference error.
The word 'peace' is misspelled as its homophone 'piece', resulting in a real-word spelling error.
The preposition 'of' is incorrectly replaced with 'for' after the adjective 'capable'.

The word 'property' is incorrectly replaced with its visually similar near-neighbor 'propriety', resulting in a semantic error since 'propriety' (correct behavior) cannot be physically removed to another country.
Changes the plural pronoun 'they' to the singular 'it', causing a disagreement with its plural antecedent 'nations'.
The plural subject 'these two objects' is incorrectly paired with the singular verb 'is', creating a subject-verb agreement error.
An apostrophe is incorrectly inserted into the plural noun 'Portions', creating an erroneous possessive form.
The word 'rights' is incorrectly replaced with its homophone 'rites', resulting in a misused word error.
Replaces 'rights' with its homophone 'rites'.
Insert an extra 'c' into 'necessary' to create the common misspelling 'neccessary'.

Removing the preposition and relative pronoun 'in which' converts the dependent relative clause into an independent clause, resulting in a comma splice where two independent clauses are joined only by a comma.
Incorrect relative pronoun case ('whom' instead of 'who' as the subject of the relative clause).
The idiom 'in general' is incorrectly blended with 'at large' to form the incorrect phrase 'in large'.
Incorrect word order: subject-auxiliary inversion is incorrectly applied in a dependent clause.
The adjective 'present' is incorrectly replaced with the adverb 'presently', resulting in a wrong word form error where an adverb modifies a noun.
Incorrect subject-verb inversion in a declarative sentence.
Removes the period between two independent clauses and lowercases the following word, creating a clear fused sentence (run-on) without any punctuation.

expectedCorrection.find: right to the use of it the utility of
expectedCorrection.replace: right to the use of it. The utility of

issues.description: Replaces the plural pronoun 'their' with the singular 'its', causing the pronoun to incorrectly refer to 'the sea' or 'use' instead of the correct entity, 'nations'.
Incorrectly splits the compound word 'wherever' into two words 'where ever'.
The count noun 'instances' is incorrectly modified by 'much', which is used for mass nouns, instead of 'many'.

expectedCorrection.replace: in as many instances as possible

issues.description: Incorrectly uses the singular form 'condition' instead of the plural 'conditions' after the plural verb 'are'.

Replacing the singular pronoun 'it' (which correctly refers to 'war') with the plural pronoun 'them' creates a pronoun reference error. 'Them' grammatically points to the nearest plural noun, 'conditions', resulting in the nonsensical meaning 'conditions necessary to render conditions just'.
Introduces a double negative by adding 'no' before 'rights' in a phrase already negated by 'no violation'.
An unmatched closing parenthesis is incorrectly inserted.

expectedCorrection.find: according to circumstances not easy to define),
expectedCorrection.replace: according to circumstances not easy to define,

issues.description: Changing the plural pronoun 'them' (which correctly refers to 'injuries') to the singular 'it' creates a pronoun reference error, as 'it' now ambiguously points to the wrong entity (such as 'nation' or 'compensation').
An unmatched quotation mark is incorrectly introduced at the beginning of the sentence.

expectedCorrection.replace: As there can be no reason why

issues.description: Omission of the closing comma for the parenthetical phrase 'in settling the difficulties of international jurisprudence'.
The object pronoun 'us' is incorrectly placed before the main verb 'enable', creating a word order error.
The preposition 'to' is omitted from the phrase 'with regard to', resulting in a grammatical error.
The relative pronoun 'which' is incorrectly changed to 'who', creating a pronoun reference error because 'who' must refer to a person, not an inanimate concept like 'parity'.

Introduces a tense inconsistency by changing the present/future modal 'may proceed' to the past tense 'proceeded', which conflicts with the hypothetical conditional 'If... we should suppose' established earlier in the sentence.
The singular subject 'property' is incorrectly paired with the plural verb 'are' due to attraction from the plural noun 'individuals'.
